name: MailAccess
description: High-throughput email OSINT investigation toolkit and domain-level mailbox harvesting engine.
how_to_use: Trace individual email handles to uncover associated accounts and breach disclosures, or harvest employee email addresses across an entire corporate domain.
command_example:
mailaccess investigate target@example.com
# Or harvest domain emails:
mailaccess harvest-emails --domain target.com
about: An open-source email intelligence engine that runs dozens of OSINT modules in parallel across breach databases, social networks, and DNS records to construct a unified identity graph with confidence scores.
who_can_use: OSINT Investigators, Corporate Security Analysts, Fraud Examiners, and Penetration Testers.

name: TorBot
description: Dark web OSINT crawler, hidden services mapper, and link tree visualizer for the Tor network.
installation: git clone https://github.com/DedSecInside/TorBot.git && cd TorBot && pip install -r requirements.txt
how_to_use: Verify if illicit marketplaces or leak sites are active, crawl dark web nodes recursively, and export relationship link trees for network graph analysis.
command_example:
python torbot -u http://<target-service>.onion --status
# Recursive crawl and save link tree:
python torbot -u http://<target-service>.onion --depth 2 --save json
about: A specialized dark web OSINT crawler designed to safely navigate, index, and analyze .onion hidden services, tracking link graphs and verifying service uptime.
who_can_use: Dark Web Threat Analysts, Cybercrime Investigators, Law Enforcement OSINT Teams, and CTI Researchers.

name: Horus
description: Multi-purpose OSINT and digital forensics assistant for unified artifact investigation and data synthesis.
installation: git clone https://github.com/6abd/horus.git && cd horus && pip install -r requirements.txt
how_to_use: Perform rapid multi-vector triage on unclassified indicators (handles, IP addresses, domains, files) from an interactive CLI before launching specialized heavyweight tools.
about: A unified Python OSINT and digital forensics assistant that combines indicator triage, metadata extraction, steganography checks, and encoding routines in a single shell.
who_can_use: Incident Responders, OSINT Analysts, Forensics Investigators, and Security Researchers.

name: Security News Scraper
description: Automated cybersecurity news aggregator, RSS harvester, and threat advisory scraper.
installation: git clone https://github.com/CarterPerez-dev/Cybersecurity-Projects.git && cd Cybersecurity-Projects/PROJECTS/intermediate/security-news-scraper && go run main.go
how_to_use: Run scheduled or on-demand sweeps across security news sites to generate structured feeds of zero-day exploits and trending CVE advisories for intelligence reports.
command_example:
go run main.go
# Or build standalone binary:
go build -o news-scraper main.go && ./news-scraper
about: A high-performance command-line scraper built in Go that automatically monitors, scrapes, and parses cybersecurity publications and vendor bulletins for CVE disclosures.
who_can_use: Threat Intelligence Analysts, Security Operations (SOC) Teams, Vulnerability Managers, and Tech Journalists.

name: Steganography Multi-Tool
description: Forensic image steganography analyzer and hidden payload detection utility.
installation: git clone https://github.com/CarterPerez-dev/Cybersecurity-Projects.git && cd Cybersecurity-Projects/PROJECTS/beginner/steganography-multi-tool && python -m venv venv && pip install -r requirements.txt
how_to_use: Inspect suspicious image files recovered during investigations for hidden data, or test covert communications channels in forensic exercises.
command_example:
python main.py --decode --image evidence.png
# Encode message:
python main.py --encode --image cover.png --output stego.png --message "Secret"
about: A digital image forensics utility designed to detect, encode, and extract concealed textual data and binary streams using Least Significant Bit (LSB) manipulation.
who_can_use: Digital Forensics Analysts, Incident Responders, Security Educators, and CTF Competitors.

name: Scapy
description: Powerful interactive packet manipulation library and network reconnaissance engine.
how_to_use: Construct custom network probes, audit firewall packet-filtering rules, trace complex network hops, or capture and dissect live promiscuous interface traffic.
command_example:
scapy
# Example TCP SYN probe:
>>> sr1(IP(dst="192.168.1.1")/TCP(dport=80, flags="S"), timeout=2)
about: The premier Python interactive packet manipulation program capable of forging, decoding, transmitting, and dissecting raw network packets for hundreds of protocols.
who_can_use: Network Engineers, Penetration Testers, Security Researchers, and Protocol Reverse Engineers.

name: Sniffnet
description: Cross-platform application to monitor and analyze Internet network traffic comfortably and multilingually.
how_to_use: Launch the GUI during investigations to audit outbound network connections from your lab workstation in real time, identify communicating country endpoints, and export pcaps.
about: A modern, cross-platform graphical network traffic monitor written in Rust that visualizes live bandwidth, connection channels, peer geographic locations, and autonomous systems.
who_can_use: Security Analysts, System Administrators, Network Engineers, and Privacy-Conscious Investigators.

name: Rveng
description: Advanced binary analysis and reverse engineering framework for executable inspection and disassembly.
installation: git clone https://github.com/CarterPerez-dev/Cybersecurity-Projects.git && cd Cybersecurity-Projects/PROJECTS/advanced/rveng && pip install -r requirements.txt
how_to_use: Disassemble unknown binary executables recovered during investigations, extract hardcoded C2 strings, and analyze import address tables (IAT) offline.
command_example:
python main.py --file target_sample.bin --disassemble
# Inspect PE headers:
python main.py --file target_sample.exe --headers
about: An advanced binary analysis and reverse engineering framework designed to disassemble executable binaries, parse PE/ELF headers, and inspect function tables.
who_can_use: Malware Analysts, Reverse Engineers, Forensics Specialists, and Security Students.

name: Containerlab
description: Declarative container-based network lab orchestration system for simulating complex network topologies.
how_to_use: Define target enterprise routing topologies in YAML and spin up simulated hardware appliances locally to validate routing paths and firewall policies harmlessly.
command_example:
sudo containerlab deploy --topo topology.clab.yml
# Inspect running topology:
sudo containerlab inspect --all
about: A declarative CLI tool that launches containerized network routing topologies using Docker and Linux namespaces to simulate multi-vendor network hardware (Cisco, Arista, Nokia, FRR).
who_can_use: Network Architects, Security Lab Builders, DevOps Engineers, and Red/Blue Teams.

name: System Design 101
description: Comprehensive visual reference and deep-dive compendium for system architecture and large-scale infrastructure design.
how_to_use: Study visual blueprints of enterprise web infrastructure (OAuth flows, reverse proxy caching, cloud load balancing) to model target digital perimeters accurately.
about: A visual encyclopedia by ByteByteGo explaining the inner architecture of large-scale distributed systems, CDNs, microservices, load balancers, and database clusters.
who_can_use: Security Architects, Infrastructure Analysts, Technical Investigators, and Systems Engineers.

name: Awesome Networking (Facyber)
description: Curated list of essential computer networking resources, protocols, packet analysis tools, and RFCs.
how_to_use: Quickly look up protocol header structures, subnetting calculations, and standard networking RFCs when analyzing infrastructure and network telemetry.
about: A curated technical directory of computer networking fundamentals, protocol specifications, RFC standards, packet analysis methodologies, and network troubleshooting tools.
who_can_use: Network Engineers, Infrastructure Analysts, Students, and Technical Intelligence Researchers.

name: Awesome Networking (Nyquist)
description: Curated index of modern network engineering tools, libraries, BGP frameworks, and performance analyzers.
how_to_use: Locate carrier-grade routing tools, Looking Glass servers, and high-performance packet capture libraries when investigating autonomous system (ASN) perimeters.
about: An advanced index of modern network engineering tools, high-speed packet capture engines (DPDK, XDP), BGP routing daemons, and internet-scale telemetry systems.
who_can_use: Telecommunications Engineers, Cloud Architects, Internet Topology Researchers, and BGP Analysts.

name: Multiplayer Networking Resources
description: Comprehensive technical index of real-time UDP network protocols, state synchronization, and packet architectures.
how_to_use: Reference low-level socket communication paradigms, lag compensation, and packet serialization when analyzing custom real-time network streams.
about: A technical repository compiling architectures, whitepapers, and protocol implementations for real-time UDP communication, packet framing, and state replication.
who_can_use: Network Protocol Reverse Engineers, Game Developers, IoT Engineers, and Security Researchers.

name: FaceCheck.ID
description: AI-powered facial recognition search engine to find social media profiles, news articles, and web appearances by photo.
how_to_use: Upload an image containing an unidentified face to locate matching public profiles, social accounts, and public record appearances with biometric confidence rankings.
command_example:
# Access web interface directly:
# Visit: https://facecheck.id

# Or query via Python API wrapper:
pip install requests
# Upload image and search biometric face matches
about: An AI-powered facial recognition search platform indexing faces from public websites, social media platforms, news articles, video thumbnails, and public mugshot registries.
who_can_use: Private Investigators, Cyber Threat Researchers, Due Diligence Analysts, and Anti-Scam Verification Specialists.

name: Robin
description: AI-powered dark web OSINT investigation tool utilizing LLMs for query refinement, intelligent filtering, and onion summarization.
how_to_use: Query dark web search engines using plain language; Robin refines the search with underground jargon, retrieves live onion links, and outputs AI-synthesized briefings.
command_example:
# Run Web UI mode via Docker (requires running Tor daemon):
docker run -d -p 5000:5000 --env-file .env apurvsg/robin:latest

# Or CLI investigation:
python robin.py --query "target company credentials" --llm gpt-4
about: An AI-augmented dark web intelligence tool that pairs Tor search engines with Large Language Models (LLMs) to automatically optimize query syntax, filter noise, and summarize findings.
who_can_use: Threat Intelligence Teams, SOC Analysts, Brand Protection Investigators, and Red Teams.

name: Airplanes.live
description: Community-driven, unfiltered live ADS-B flight tracking platform providing global aircraft telemetry and route histories.
how_to_use: Track state VIP transports, military aircraft, and corporate jets by registration or ICAO hex code without censorship, or query the live REST API for regional airframes.
command_example:
# Access web radar: https://airplanes.live

# Query aircraft by ICAO hex code:
curl -s "https://api.airplanes.live/v2/hex/a1b2c3" | jq .
about: An open, unfiltered flight tracking service powered by a global volunteer ADS-B radio network that provides raw, uncensored telemetry for civil and military aircraft worldwide.
who_can_use: Aviation OSINT Researchers, Investigative Journalists, Geopolitical Analysts, and Defense Observers.

name: TruffleHog
description: High-performance secrets scanner for finding and verifying leaked credentials, private keys, and API tokens across git history, filesystems, and cloud endpoints.
how_to_use: Scan target organization code repositories and cloud buckets to uncover accidentally exposed credentials and verify active permissions without manual testing.
command_example:
# Scan a public git repository for exposed secrets:
trufflehog git https://github.com/target/repo.git

# Scan an entire GitHub organization:
trufflehog github --org=targetorg
about: A high-speed security scanner that detects secrets, private keys, passwords, and API tokens across git histories, filesystems, and S3 buckets, actively verifying if they are live.
who_can_use: AppSec Engineers, External Attack Surface Analysts, Red Teamers, and Penetration Testers.
